chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih al-Thawri, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Ali عليه السلام used to say: “Whoever we strike with a hadd punishment from among the hudud of Allah and then he dies, there is no diyah for him upon us. But whoever we strike with a hadd punishment regarding something from the rights of the people and then he dies, then indeed his diyah is upon us.”

key_terms.حُدُودِ اللَّهِ: the divinely ordained penal limits and punishments
key_terms.حُقُوقِ النَّاسِ: the rights and claims belonging to human beings
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood money or legal compensation for wrongful death

ai.seo_question: Is diyah required if someone dies while receiving a hadd punishment in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal distinction between punishments carried out as the hudud of Allah and punishments connected to the rights of people. If death occurs in the former, no diyah is due, while in the latter, diyah remains payable, reflecting the legal weight of human rights in adjudication.
